title: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)

sections.label: Parliamentary Motion on climate change
sections.summary: The House declared climate change a global emergency and committed to mitigation, adaptation and sustainability, with a Singapore Green Plan 2030 launched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last month, my Government Parliamentary Committees (GPC) colleagues and I delivered the first ever Parliamentary Motion on climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This House declared climate change a global emergency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We committed to deepening and accelerating efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change and to embrace sustainability in our development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened that we are making progress and have launched a Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sections.label: Cities pledging net-zero emissions
sections.summary: Several cities including Hong Kong, Monaco and Delhi have pledged to work towards net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Several cities such as Hong Kong, Monaco, Delhi have pledged to work towards net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.

sections.label: Question on Singapore net-zero pledge
sections.summary: It asks whether Singapore will pledge to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 and what its plans are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Will Singapore also pledge to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050, and what are our plans to achieve this goal?

sections.label: Singapore's 2015 Paris Agreement commitment
sections.summary: In 2015 Singapore committed to reduce emission intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030 and stabilise greenhouse emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In 2015, in line with the Paris Agreement, Singapore made further commitment to reduce our emission intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030 and to stabilise our greenhouse emissions aiming to peak at around 230.

sections.label: Singapore solar target 2030
sections.summary: Singapore has set a solar target of 2 gigawatt-peak by 2030, enough power for over 300,000 homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Singapore has set an ambitious solar target of "2 gigawatt-peak by 2030", which will provide enough power for over 300,000 homes.

sections.label: Electricity imports from Malaysia
sections.summary: Last year the Government announced plans to import 100 megawatts of electricity from Malaysia for two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Last year, the Government announced plans to import 100 megawatts of electricity from Malaysia for two years.

sections.label: Carbon tax climate strategy
sections.summary: Asks how an increased carbon tax will impact Singapore's climate strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How will an increased in carbon tax impact our climate strategy?

sections.label: Next NDC emissions target
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government intends to set a more ambitious emissions target for the next NDC submission due by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, the aim to green 80% of all buildings over the next decade is a target that was set in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As I mentioned during the Debate on the Climate Change Motion, Singapore's updated NDC targets submitted in 2020 does not genuinely limit emissions growth beyond what was already committed to under our first NDC, which was submitted in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The next NDC's submission is due by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Does the Government intend for Singapore to set more ambitious emissions target for this next submission?

sections.label: Singapore Green Plan 2030 vision
sections.summary: Describes the Singapore Green Plan 2030 as a vision and rallying cry for Singapore to become a sustainable Smart Nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Green Plan or SGP2030, is an exciting vision and a rallying cry for the whole of Singapore to work towards becoming a sustainable Smart Nation.

sections.label: Companies aligning with SGP2030
sections.summary: States companies can align with SGP2030 to comply with targets, join the green economy and gain competitive advantage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our companies will all have an opportunity to get on this agenda, and align with SGP2030 to: one, ensure that they themselves will be able to comply with the targets; two, that their business will be ready to participate in the global "green" economy when buyers of products and services will be calling for "green" criteria to be met; and three, that sustainability will become the differentiator and competitive advantage and new businesses and start-ups will be conceived.

sections.label: MSE assessment programme question
sections.summary: Asks whether MSE will develop and roll out an assessment programme like the SERI for Industry 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will MSE be developing and rolling out an assessment programme, much like the SERI for Industry 4.0?

sections.label: Sea level rise protection plans
sections.summary: Asks what plans exist to protect Singapore against sea level rise projected to increase by about one metre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On the matter of global warming, what are our plans to protect Singapore against the threat of sea level rise?

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is especially so since our sea level is projected to further increase by about one metre.

sections.label: City in Nature targets
sections.summary: City in Nature targets include doubling annual tree planting, increasing nature park land by over 50%, and adding 1,000 hectares of green spaces.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The targets of City in Nature include doubling our annual tree planting rate, increasing the land area of our nature parks by over 50%, and adding 1,000 hectares of green spaces.

sections.label: Singapore natural capital engagement
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee announced engaging the nature community to map island-wide eco-systems and connectivity and understand how sites connect to nature cores, buffers and corridors.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What more can we do by leveraging Singapore's natural capital to strengthen our ecological, climate and socio-economic resilience?

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is why I am excited by Minister Desmond Lee’s recent announcement to engage the nature community in building a more comprehensive picture of Singapore’s island-wide eco-systems and connectivity, and in understanding how specific sites connect to our nature cores, buffers and corridors.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Ministry's plan to do this in a scientific and systematic manner is extremely important and a huge step forward for us to understand the value of green spaces in the broader context of Singapore's natural capital at the national scale.

sections.label: Kranji Woodland incident investigations
sections.summary: The speaker is confident ongoing investigations by relevant agencies will identify gaps or breaches that may have caused the premature land clearance.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With regards to the Kranji Woodland incident, I am confident that ongoing investigations by the relevant agencies will identify any gaps or breaches that may have resulted in the premature land clearance.

sections.label: Kranji environmental monitoring plan
sections.summary: The question asks how the environmental monitoring and management plan for Kranji will mitigate ecological impact on Sungei Pang Sua and neighbouring habitats.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How do we ensure that the environmental monitoring and management plan for Kranji will deliver its intended outcome of mitigating any ecological impact on Sungei Pang Sua and neighbouring habitats, such as Mandai mangrove and mudflat?

sections.label: Centralising EIA processes
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee's announcement to explore centralising EIA processes is described as a significant and positive step.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recent announcement by Minister Desmond Lee to explore the potential of centralising EIA processes is another significant and positive step in the right direction.

sections.label: Developer burden for impacts
sections.summary: The speaker suggests developers should first show no impacts beyond acceptable thresholds, and if unavoidable, demonstrate adequate mitigation measures.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps the initial burden should instead rest on the developer, to always be required to show, prior to development, that there would not be impacts beyond acceptable thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And if there would be potentially unavoidable impacts, to require the developer to put in place and demonstrate the adequacy of mitigation measures.

sections.label: Climate-resilient urban infrastructure planning
sections.summary: It states that adopting existing climate change information and resources for urban planning is imperative to make urban infrastructures more climate-resilient.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: To ensure that urban infrastructures are more climate-resilient, it is imperative to adopt the use of existing climate change information and resources for urban planning.

sections.label: Sustainability guidelines for developments
sections.summary: It asks whether the Ministry will legislate that future public or private developments align with sustainability guidelines, and notes stakeholders will co-create the next Green Building Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Will the Ministry legislate the requirement for future public or private developments to align with certain sustainability guidelines in the design process?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: At Committee of Supply 2020, it was announced that various stakeholders will be invited to co-create the next edition of Green Building Masterplan.

sections.label: South Korea smart farm project
sections.summary: It cites South Korea's Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs launching a US$36 million project to research, develop and demonstrate smart farm technologies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Let us take a leaf from other countries like in South Korea where the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs is launching a US$36 million project to research, develop and demonstrate smart farm technologies and the next-generation core and convergence techs.

sections.label: Standardising green finance accounting standards
sections.summary: It states that the accounting standards framework should be standardised to further grow green finance.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Second, to standardise the accounting standards framework to further grow the green finance.

sections.label: Standardised accounting framework for green finance
sections.summary: It states a standardised accounting framework would enable interpretation and comparison of emissions and transparency, and cites a paper concurring on benefits for ASEAN's green finance sector.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Locally, having a standardised accounting framework would better enable meaningful interpretation and comparison of emissions as well as allowing for greater transparency of these green investments.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: In the Green Finance Position Paper 2020 by Eurocham Singapore and Accenture, the paper also concurred on the benefits of having a standardised accounting standards framework for the region in further growing the green finance sector for ASEAN.

sections.label: HDB Green Towns Programme update
sections.summary: It asks for an update on the HDB Green Towns Programme announced at last year's Committee of Supply, and notes about one in three MacPherson residents are aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: On this note, I would like to ask for an update on the progress of the HDB Green Towns Programme which was announced at last year's Committee of Supply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In MacPherson, about one in three of our residents are aged 60 and above.

sections.label: Lift breakdowns in public housing
sections.summary: Lifts break down regularly despite monthly maintenance because of high daily usage and ageing lifts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: One pain-point faced is the regular breakdown of lifts, despite monthly maintenance scheduled because of high daily usage and lifts being aged.

sections.label: Electricity use in mature estates
sections.summary: EMA data shows public housing electricity consumption in mature estates is about 10% higher than non-mature ones over 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In addition, based on EMA's data, electricity consumption of public housing in mature estates is about 10% higher than that of non-mature ones over the past 15 years.

sections.label: Solar cost stability and Solar Nova
sections.summary: Solar costs are fixed upfront and spread over 20 to 25 years, so stepping up Solar Nova can achieve cleaner living sooner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For solar, the cost is fixed and locked in upfront and then spread over a fixed term of 20 to 25 years, thereby offering cost stability and predictability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, if we can step up the implementation of Solar Nova, especially for mature estates, before the 2030 target, we can achieve a cleaner and greener living sooner.

sections.label: NParks four key strategies
sections.summary: NParks announced four strategies: extending nature park network, intensifying nature and gardens, restoring nature into built environment, and strengthening green space connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: In the announcement, NParks shared four key strategies: extending our nature park network, intensifying nature and gardens and parks, restoring nature into the built environment and strengthening connectivity between our green spaces.

sections.label: Schools reducing energy and waste
sections.summary: It asks what efforts schools can make to reduce campus energy use and waste, and what Government support measures will be extended.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: What efforts can schools embark on to reduce energy usage and waste generation on campus?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: And in light of the recent announcement that 20% of schools will be carbon neutral by 2030, what are some of the support measures that the Government will extend for this goal to be reached?

sections.label: MSE sustainability talent scholarships
sections.summary: MSE's 2020 Addendum stated the Minister said MSE will develop sustainability talent through scholarships in areas like climate adaptation and climate science.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In MSE's Addendum to the President's Address in 2020, the Minister stated that MSE will develop a pipeline of talent to support sustainability in Singapore, by offering scholarships in specified areas, such as climate adaptation and climate science.

sections.label: Green Purpose sustainability webinar
sections.summary: Journey of a Green Purpose is a 12-part webinar by Seastainable and Green Nudge Singapore equipping students and young adults for sustainability careers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One example of a programme that could be expanded is "Journey of a Green Purpose", an initiative spearheaded by Seastainable and Green Nudge Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a 12-part webinar that aims to equip students and young adults with knowledge on what to consider while trying to establish a career in sustainability.

sections.label: Singapore Green Plan school target
sections.summary: The Singapore Green Plan aims to get at least 20% of schools carbon neutral by 2030, with the rest to follow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: To this end, the Singapore Green Plan aims to enhance environmental sustainability in schools and get at least 20% of schools here to be carbon neutral by 2030, with the rest to follow thereafter.

sections.label: Budget for electric vehicle initiatives
sections.summary: $30 million is set aside in this year's Budget for electric vehicle related initiatives over the next five years, which can only be a start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: In this light, the $30 million set aside in this year's Budget for electric vehicle related initiatives over the next five years, can only be a start.

sections.label: EV charging point target question
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry decided on the target of 60,000 EV charging points by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: How did the Ministry decide on the target of 60,000 EV charging points by 2030?

sections.label: EV battery recycling and car pricing
sections.summary: The passage asks about sustainable disposal and recycling of EV batteries and urges lower taxes on electric or hybrid cars to encourage buyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have plans to ensure the sustainable disposal and recycling of EV batteries?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I wanted to do my small part to buy a car which uses less petrol and hence be environmentally more friendly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, at the car dealer, I was told that the hybrid version of the car would cost almost $10,000 more than the petrol model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, while I applaud the intent of the Government to move towards cleaner energy car models, we need to take a holistic view at the pricing of cars such that we can effectively encourage car buyers to opt for cleaner energy cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, the Government should look at lowering taxes on electric cars or hybrid cars so that a similar model would either be less expensive than an internal combustion engine vehicle or at least on par in terms of pricing.

sections.label: Compulsory charging points in car parks
sections.summary: The passage urges LTA to make it compulsory for HDB car parks, condominiums and office buildings to provide a minimum number of charging points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Without available charging points for their Electric Vehicles, many drivers will be concerned as to how they charge their Electric Vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, I urge LTA to make it compulsory for HDB car parks, for condominiums and even office buildings to provide a minimum number of charging points in the car parks.

sections.label: Tesla Model 3 cost
sections.summary: The basic Tesla Model 3 will cost about $160,000 including the current COE price, equivalent to a BMW 2 series or Mercedes A Class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, the basic Tesla Model 3 will cost about $160,000, inclusive of the current COE price, which is equivalent to the BMW 2 series or the Mercedes A Class.

sections.label: 60,000 charging points target
sections.summary: The Government has set a target of installing 60,000 charging points islandwide by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government has set a target of installing 60,000 charging points islandwide by 2030.

sections.label: Intermediate milestones for vehicle targets
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry considered intermediate milestones as indicators of success towards the 2030 and 2040 cleaner energy vehicle targets.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
sentences.text: Additionally, has the Ministry considered any intermediate milestones as indicators of success towards achieving the 2030 target of requiring all newly registered vehicles to be of cleaner energy models, and the 2040 target of having only cleaner energy vehicles on the road?

sections.label: EMA electricity import trial
sections.summary: The EMA is embarking on a two-year trial for electricity imports from Malaysia to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin
sentences.text: In fact, the EMA is embarking on a two-year trial for electricity imports from Malaysia to Singapore.

sections.label: Electricity from natural gas
sections.summary: About 95% of our electricity is generated from natural gas sources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we speak, about 95% of our electricity is generated from natural gas sources.

sections.label: Data centre greenhouse gas emissions
sections.summary: Data centres worldwide account for around 2% of greenhouse gas emissions, expected to surge to 14% by 2040, the same as the US share today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Collectively, data centres around the world account for around 2% of greenhouse gas emissions and is expected to surge to 14% by 2040, the same as the US share of global emissions today.

sections.label: Oil and gas job outlook
sections.summary: MP asks for the Government's expected jobs outlook for oil, gas and petrochemicals amid decarbonisation, citing Shell and ExxonMobil job cuts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Last year, Shell announced its intent to axe 500 jobs or 38% of its Pulau Bukom workforce and aims to reduce its global workforce by up to 9,000 by 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Just today, ExxonMobil announced that it will be cutting 7% of jobs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a Parliamentary reply to my Parliamentary colleague, Ms He Ting Ru, MTI said that the shift to low emissions mobility would not result in significant job losses for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But can the Government share its expected outlook for jobs in the oil and gas and petrochemicals industry clusters as a result of the longer term global decarbonisation trend?

sections.label: Green economy jobs and skills review
sections.summary: MP asks whether a strategic review of in-demand green economy jobs and skills, and of impacted local jobs, has or will be done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This will help make climate change relevant and relevant to the broader community, not just a fortunate few and rally them to join in the conversation and more important action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: That that end, I would like to ask if a strategic review of the jobs and skills that will be in demand in the green economy has or will be done along with a review of the jobs, particularly local jobs that will be impacted directly or indirectly by the transition to the green economy.

sections.label: ESG mark for Singapore
sections.summary: MP calls on the Government to introduce an ESG mark with indicators applicable to Singapore and Asia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In addition, I spoke about how enterprises are agents to societal changes and we need more companies be created with missions that value adds to our society and improves our societal well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is possible and I call on the Government to implement ESG for SG, in other words, introduce an ESG mark with clear and appropriate indicators for environmental, social and governance that is applicable to Singapore and Asia.

sections.label: Dovetailing marks into ESG mark
sections.summary: MP recommends dovetailing BCA Green Mark, Enabling Mark and PWM Mark into a larger ESG mark for one benchmarking standard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Apart from the above proposal, I recommend that we dovetail existing and future measurements, such as BCA Green Mark, Enabling Mark, PWM Mark as part of a larger ESG mark so the Enterprises have one clear benchmarking standard and investors and consumers have only one report to assess the companies from its peers.

sections.label: ESG in Enterprise Grant evaluation
sections.summary: MP proposes incorporating an ESG component in the evaluation of Enterprise Grant schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With this in mind, I propose that we take a small step but incorporating a ESG component in the evaluation of Enterprise Grant schemes.

sections.label: Support for SMEs' green capabilities
sections.summary: MP asks whether additional SME support will be provided beyond the Enterprise Sustainability Programme and whether funds for trialling green technologies will be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Government has introduced the Enterprise Sustainability Programme to help enterprises, especially that of SMEs, to grow their green capabilities and benefit from the new opportunities in the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share whether we will be providing additional support to the SMEs on top of what is provided under the programme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can the Government also consider support and funds to companies that want to trial or introduce new green technologies to their current business operations?

sections.label: Carbon capture and reclamation level
sections.summary: Passage asks MSE for an update on a 2020 carbon capture MOU and notes Singapore raised minimum reclamation level in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: A balanced approach will, therefore, be to acknowledge that Singapore provides essential manufacturing services, including petrochemicals to the rest of the world, and the way we discharge our duty to the world is to ensure that our companies achieve world-class efficiencies in energy and carbon." On this note, can I get MSE to provide an update on the progress of the Memorandum of Understanding signed in July 2020 by Chevron, Pan-United, Keppel Data Centres and Surbana Jurong, with the support of Singapore's National Research Foundation regarding the aspiration and development of mature carbon capture, utilisation and storage technologies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To meet the expected long-term sea level rise, the minimum land reclamation level in Singapore was raised from three to four metres above mean sea level in 2011.

sections.label: Hundred billion dollar investments
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said these will be huge investments up to $100 billion requiring long-term planning up to 100 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Prime Minister mentioned that these will be huge investments amounting up to $100 billion and we need to long-term planning up to a 100 years.

sections.label: PUB coastal protection agency
sections.summary: Passage welcomes PUB as Coastal Protection Agency in 2020 and asks what coastal adaptation solutions and nature-based solutions will be examined.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The announcement of the PUB assuming the role of the nation's Coastal Protection Agency in 2020 is heartening, as efforts are coordinated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What are some examples of coastal adaptation solutions that will be examined under the site specific studies mentioned and to what extent will nature based solutions be considered as we must be careful about reclamation.

sections.label: November flash floods
sections.summary: Last November flash floods occurred in three areas and water levels rose to 90% of capacity in eight other locations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Just last November, flash floods occurred in three areas and water levels in drains and canals rose to 90% of their capacity in eight other locations.

sections.label: BCA Coastal Adaptation Study update
sections.summary: Passage asks the Minister for an update on measures undertaken since the BCA Coastal Adaptation Study concluded in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Since the BCA Coastal Adaptation Study was concluded in 2019, can Minister provide an update on the measures undertaken in response to this study?

sections.label: Contingency for coinciding flood conditions
sections.summary: Passage asks whether contingency measures exist should heavy downpour, high tide and maximum canal capacity coincide.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Do we have any contingency measures in place should an incessant heavy downpour coupled with high tide conditions and maximum canal holding capacity coincide?

sections.label: Urban heat and global warming
sections.summary: Asks how Singapore's urban temperature will rise from global warming and how this would worsen the UHI effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How will Singapore's urban temperature rise as a result of global warming, and how would this exacerbate the UHI effect?

sections.label: Company-level emissions disclosures
sections.summary: The German Institute of Economic Research found company-level disclosures work, reducing emissions by 17% permanently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The German Institute of Economic Research has found that such company-level disclosures work, reducing emissions by 17% permanently.

sections.label: Smart Nation and e-waste
sections.summary: As Singapore pursues its Smart Nation initiative, it must manage e-waste, generating more than 60,000 tonnes annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As Singapore pursues its Smart Nation initiative, we must also be smart about how we manage our e-waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We generate more than 60,000 tonnes of e-waste annually.

sections.label: E-waste recycling and EPR framework
sections.summary: The Government has built up e-waste recycling facilities, and MSE announced the Extended Producer Responsibility framework for e-waste from July this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the Government has been building up its e-waste recycling facilities and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have been raising this issue in Parliament since 2016 and I am glad that MSE announced that the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework for e-waste will be implemented from July this year.

sections.label: Food waste generated in 2019
sections.summary: In 2019, Singapore generated over 700,000 tonnes of food waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2019, we generated over 700,000 tonnes of food waste.

sections.label: Plastic recycling rate
sections.summary: Physical recycling is the main channel to reuse plastic, but the current recycling rate of only 4% for plastics is poor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Physical recycling is the main channel to reuse plastic, but our current recycling rate of only 4% for plastics is poor.

sections.label: Plastic bag global warming research
sections.summary: NTU and Finland researchers found single-use plastic bags have 14 times more global warming potential than a reusable plastic bag.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: To put matters in perspective, a recent research by researchers from NTU and their colleagues in Finland has shown how single-use plastic bags have a global warming potential 14 times more than a reusable plastic bag.

sections.label: Toilet renovation grant conditions
sections.summary: Town Councils must complete approved toilet renovation works by 31 March 2022, and the grant quantum is reduced if a hawker centre smoking corner is not removed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

sections.label: Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund
sections.summary: The new $60 million ACT Fund replaces the APF that expired in 2020 and funds local farms over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The new $60 million Agri-Food Cluster Transformation (ACT) Fund replaces the APF which expired in 2020 and provides funding support for local farms over the next five years.

sections.label: Farms with expiring leases
sections.summary: Twenty-six farms with expiring leases can stay until their leases expire, most with a further short extension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Twenty-six farms have leases expiring and will be able to stay on until their leases expire, with most having a further short extension.

sections.label: Lim Chu Kang agri-food zone
sections.summary: SFA announced in October 2020 it will master-plan about 390 hectares in Lim Chu Kang into a high-tech agri-food zone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: SFA announced in October 2020 that it will be master-planning about 390 hectares of land in Lim Chu Kang and transform this area into a high-tech agri-food zone.

sections.label: Cultured chicken and novel foods
sections.summary: SFA allowed EAT Just, Inc. to sell cultured chicken nuggets, and the new Act mandates pre-market safety assessment for novel foods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Last December, SFA allowed the company EAT Just, Inc. to sell its cultured chicken as an ingredient in nuggets in Singapore after rigorously assessing that all food safety risks have been addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The new Act will provide greater legal clarity on the regulatory framework for novel foods, including mandating that a pre-market safety assessment must be done before approval for sale is granted.

sections.label: Food delivery food safety responsibility
sections.summary: Food delivery companies are not licensed by SFA but must transport food without compromising safety, and SFA engages them on practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: While food delivery companies are not licensed by SFA as they are not involved in the food preparation or processing and thus have minimal risks of causing food contamination, they remain responsible for ensuring that the food is transported in a manner that does not compromise on food safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: This includes maintaining the cleanliness of the vehicle and equipment used for the transportation of food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: SFA has been engaging food delivery companies on food safety practices and will explore Ms Nadia Samdin’s suggestion for these companies to indicate hygiene and cleanliness information on their platform.

sections.label: Hawker Development Programme progress
sections.summary: Under the Hawker Development Programme, 200 went through training, 66 completed apprenticeship, 46 seek stalls, and new hawker centres are being built.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, for our Hawker Development Programme (HDP) that we recently initiated, 200 have actually gone through the training programme, 66 have completed the apprenticeship, 46 are now looking for stalls to start their incubation stall phase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Indeed, even as we have built seven new hawker centres, 13 are coming up, 10 are actually in design and construction, one is in the planning stage, the other two we have not announced the details.

sections.label: Hawker Succession Programme veteran mentors
sections.summary: The Hawker Succession Programme lets retiring veteran hawkers pass culinary skills and recipes to new hawkers, with 70 veteran hawkers mentoring.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Recently, we announced the Hawker Succession Programme that is actually for veteran hawkers who want to retire and we do not have anyone to take over the stalls and they do not mind passing on their culinary skills and recipes to a new breed of hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have 70 veteran hawkers who are actually mentoring our new breed of hawkers.

sections.label: Increase in generation demand
sections.summary: The increase in generation demand is estimated to be about 600 to 1,200 megawatts-peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The increase in generation demand is estimated to be about 600 to 1,200 megawatts-peak.

sections.label: Charging stations electricity pricing
sections.summary: Charging stations in Singapore buy from the grid, pay grid charges, add installation cost and margin, and sell electricity at 39 to 50 cents per kilowatt hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: You do find these charging stations around in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They buy from the grid, pay grid charges and then add to their installation cost plus their margin, they are able to sell electricity at 39 cents to 50 cents per kilowatt hour.

sections.label: PUB minimum labelling requirements consultation
sections.summary: PUB consulted the industry extensively on minimum labelling requirements and assesses minimal impact in compliance costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: PUB has consulted the industry quite extensively on these minimum labelling requirements and we assess that the requirements will have minimal impact in terms of compliance costs.

sections.label: WC flush valve replacement requirement
sections.summary: The mandatory requirement applies only if consumers buy a new WC flush valve or replace existing non water-efficient ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Just to also answer the Member's portion on whether those who are on one-tick, would they need to be replaced, the mandatory requirement will only apply if consumers wish to purchase new WC flush valve or replace their existing non water-efficient ones.

sections.label: Technologies including battery swapping
sections.summary: From now to 2030, more technologies, including battery swapping, can still be seen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: From now to 2030, you can still see more technologies, including battery swapping.

sections.label: No-regrets EV infrastructure move
sections.summary: Using existing spare capacity and last-mile installation charges is a no-regrets move based on current trajectory and technological advancement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, I think it is something that we can ride on and start to develop the infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And if you follow my speech just now, we are not going big guns and build a huge infrastructure that can bear the risks of being stranded should technology move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, if we use existing spare capacity, install last-mile installation charges, I do not think we are at great risk of any stranded technology risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, I think it is a no-regrets move based on current trajectory, based on current technological advancement, based on the fact that, in a few years' time, we are going to see parity between EVs that are based on charging, and ICE vehicles.
